about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Burmese Mohinga Fish and Lemongrass Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: Burma's breakfast soup of thick fish and lemongrass broth over rice noodles with boiled egg and lime.
steps: Simmer the fish, water, lemongrass and ginger for 8 minutes, until the fish flakes, then lift out the fish and flake the meat, discarding bones and skin.
Fry the onion, garlic and turmeric in the oil for 6 minutes, until golden and fragrant.
Toast the chickpea flour in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then whisk it into the broth with the fried onion mix.
Simmer the broth for 20 minutes, until thickened enough to coat a spoon, then season with the fish sauce.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool, peel and halve, and soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, until soft.
Serve the noodles in bowls with the fish, egg, broth, shallots, coriander and lime.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set.
Add chilli flakes at the table.

recipes.title: Thai Khao Soi Style Coconut Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: Northern Thai coconut curry noodle soup with chicken, crispy noodles, pickled mustard greens and lime.
steps: Fry the curry paste, turmeric and curry powder in 1 tbsp oil for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 4 minutes, until lightly browned.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through at 75°C and the broth is rich.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar.
Fry the 50g noodles in the remaining oil for 1 minute, until puffed and golden, and drain on paper towel.
Boil the remaining noodles for 3 minutes, until tender, drain and divide between bowls.
Ladle over the soup and top with the crispy noodles, spring onion, pickles and lime.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C in the thickest part with no pink inside.
Use tofu and vegetable stock for a vegetarian bowl.

recipes.title: Chinese Egg Drop Soup with Sweetcorn
recipes.summary: Silky ribbons of egg in a gingery chicken broth with sweetcorn, white pepper and spring onion.
steps: Simmer the stock and ginger for 5 minutes, until fragrant, then remove the ginger.
Add the sweetcorn and soy sauce and simmer for 3 minutes, until tender.
Mix the cornflour and water, stir into the soup and cook for 1 minute, until slightly thickened.
Stir the soup in one direction and pour in the eggs in a thin stream, so they form ribbons.
Switch off the heat, then add the sesame oil, spring onion and white pepper.
notes: Food safety: make sure the egg is fully set in the simmering broth before serving.
Use vegetable stock for a vegetarian version.

recipes.title: Japanese Zosui Egg and Rice Soup
recipes.summary: A gentle dashi and soy rice porridge with soft-set egg, ginger and spring onion, ideal for slow mornings.
steps: Rinse the cooked rice under hot water to remove the starch, then drain.
Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and salt to a simmer in a saucepan, until steaming.
Add the rice and simmer for 8 minutes, until the grains are soft and the broth slightly thick.
Pour in the egg in a thin circle, cover for 1 minute off the heat, until just set.
Top with ginger, spring onion and nori.
notes: Food safety: cook the egg until it is fully set before serving.
Check the dashi for fish if you need a vegetarian bowl.

recipes.title: Italian Pasta e Ceci Chickpea and Rosemary Soup
recipes.summary: Rustic Roman chickpea and small pasta soup with rosemary, garlic and a drizzle of good olive oil.
steps: Cook the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and rosemary for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas and stock and simmer for 12 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Mash a third of the chickpeas against the pot to thicken.
Add the pasta and simmer for 8 minutes, until al dente, adding water if too thick.
Season and serve with the remaining oil.
notes: Remove the rosemary stalks before serving.
Add a splash of water on reheating, as the pasta absorbs liquid.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Tuscan White Bean and Kale Soup
recipes.summary: A thick brothy soup of white beans, kale, garlic and tomato, with a slice of toasted bread underneath.

items: 1 bunch kale, stems removed and leaves sliced

steps: Cook the onion, carrots and garlic in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, beans and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Mash a quarter of the beans against the pot to thicken the broth.
Add the kale and simmer for 8 minutes, until tender but still green.
Toast the bread until golden and crisp, then place in bowls.
Ladle the soup over, season with the salt and finish with the remaining oil.
notes: Keeps 4 days and tastes better the next day.

recipes.title: Spanish Fabada Style White Bean Soup with Chorizo
recipes.summary: A hearty white bean and chorizo soup coloured with smoked paprika, cooked low until creamy.
steps: Fry the chorizo in the oil for 5 minutes, until it releases its fat and crisps slightly.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the paprika, then add the drained beans, bay leaf, saffron and water.
Simmer gently for 50 minutes, until the beans are completely tender and creamy.
Season with the salt, remove the bay leaf and serve.
notes: Food safety: cook the chorizo until 75°C in the centre and piping hot; boil dried beans vigorously for 10 minutes in fresh water before simmering to destroy toxins.
Skip the chorizo for a vegan soup and add extra paprika.

recipes.title: Greek Fakes Lentil Soup with Vinegar and Oregano
recipes.summary: Everyday Greek brown lentil soup, simmered with bay and garlic and finished with red wine vinegar and olive oil.
steps: Cook the onion, carrot and garlic in 2 tbsp oil for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, bay leaves and water and simmer for 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender and the soup thick.
Season with the salt and stir in the vinegar.
Serve with the remaining oil poured over.
notes: Serve with feta and olives for a fuller meal.

recipes.title: Ukrainian Green Borscht with Spinach and Egg
recipes.summary: A sharp, lemony green borscht of potato, spinach and dill, topped with a boiled egg and a spoon of sour cream.
steps: Cook the onion and carrot in the butter for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the stock and potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool, peel and halve.
Stir the spinach into the soup for 2 minutes, until just wilted, then add the dill, lemon juice and salt.
Serve topped with the eggs and sour cream.
notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set.
Use vegetable stock for a vegetarian soup.

recipes.title: Spiced Chickpea Flour Stew with Paprika and Ginger
recipes.summary: A smooth, spiced chickpea flour stew with onion, garlic and paprika, served with injera or rice.
steps: Cook the onion in a dry pot for 5 minutes, until softened, then add the oil, garlic and ginger and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, cumin and cardamom for 1 minute.
Whisk the chickpea flour into the water until smooth, then pour it into the pot.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and smooth.
Season with the salt and lemon juice.
notes: Whisk constantly as you add the flour to prevent lumps.
Serve with bread or rice.

recipes.title: South African Split Pea and Ham Soup
recipes.summary: A thick winter soup of green split peas, a smoky ham hock and root vegetables, served with buttered bread.
steps: Place the ham hock, split peas, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, bay leaves and water in a large pot.
Bring to the boil, skim the surface, then simmer for 75 minutes, until the peas have collapsed and the ham is very tender.
Lift out the hock and shred the meat, discarding skin and bones.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 12 minutes, until tender.
Return the meat to the pot, season with the pepper and thin with water if needed.
notes: Food safety: cool leftovers within 2 hours and keep for up to 3 days.
The hock is salty, so taste before adding salt.

recipes.title: Mexican Caldo de Pollo
recipes.summary: A homely Mexican chicken soup with corn, carrots, potatoes and zucchini, served with coriander, onion and lime.
steps: Simmer the chicken, water, halved onion, garlic and salt for 30 minutes, skimming, until the chicken is cooked through at 75°C.
Lift out the chicken and shred the meat, discarding skin and bones.
Add the carrots, potatoes and corn to the broth and simmer for 12 minutes, until almost tender.
Add the zucchini and simmer for 5 minutes, until just soft.
Return the chicken to the pot and serve with coriander, chopped onion and lime.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C in the thickest part with no pink inside; chill leftovers within 2 hours.
Add a chopped chilli for heat.

recipes.title: Chilean Cazuela de Pollo with Pumpkin and Corn
recipes.summary: A whole-meal Chilean chicken soup with a big piece of pumpkin, potato, corn and rice, finished with coriander.
steps: Simmer the chicken, onion, garlic, paprika and water for 20 minutes, skimming.
Add the pumpkin, potatoes and corn and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the rice and capsicum and simmer for 12 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through at 75°C.
Season with the salt and serve with the coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C at the bone and the juices run clear.
Use a pumpkin with firm flesh so it holds its shape.

recipes.title: Argentinian Locro Style Pumpkin and Bean Stew
recipes.summary: A thick, hearty stew of white beans, pumpkin, corn and chorizo that warms the Andes in winter.
steps: Boil the drained beans in fresh water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Fry the bacon and chorizo in the oil for 6 minutes, until the fat runs and they are lightly browned.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the paprika.
Add the beans and water and simmer for 40 minutes, until the beans are nearly tender.
Add the pumpkin and corn and simmer for 15 minutes, until the pumpkin starts to break down and the stew is thick.
Season with the salt and serve with the spring onion.
notes: Food safety: cook the chorizo until 75°C in the centre and piping hot; boil dried beans for at least 10 minutes before simmering.
Mash some of the pumpkin to thicken.

recipes.title: Ecuadorian Locro de Papa Potato and Cheese Soup
recipes.summary: A creamy Andean potato soup with milk and soft cheese, served with avocado and a crunchy side of corn.
steps: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the cumin and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and water and simmer for 20 minutes, until very soft.
Mash roughly with a potato masher, then add the milk and warm through for 3 minutes.
Season with the salt and serve topped with the queso fresco, avocado and spring onion.
notes: Mash fully for a smooth soup.
Use feta if you cannot find queso fresco.

recipes.title: Canadian Split Pea Soup with Smoked Ham
recipes.summary: A thick Quebec-style yellow split pea soup with smoky ham, carrot, celery and thyme.
steps: Place the peas, ham, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, thyme, bay leaves and water in a large pot.
Bring to the boil, skim the surface, then simmer for 70 minutes, stirring often, until the peas have collapsed and the soup is thick.
Remove the thyme and bay leaves.
Season with the pepper, adding water if too thick.
notes: Food safety: cool leftovers within 2 hours and keep up to 3 days.
Taste before adding salt, as the ham is salty.

recipes.title: New England Corn Chowder
recipes.summary: A creamy chowder of sweetcorn, potato and bacon, thickened with milk and finished with chives.
steps: Cook the bacon in a pot for 6 minutes, until crisp, then lift out half and keep for topping.
Cook the onion and celery in the bacon fat for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually add the stock.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until tender.
Add the corn, milk and cream and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick.
Season with the pepper and serve with the reserved bacon and chives.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and piping hot.
Blend a third of the soup for a thicker chowder.

recipes.title: Hawaiian Saimin Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: Hawai'i's comfort noodle soup: wheat noodles in a clear dashi and pork broth with ham, egg and spring onion.
steps: Simmer the stock, dashi, soy sauce, sugar and ginger for 10 minutes, until fragrant.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool, peel and halve.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Divide the noodles between bowls and top with ham and fish cake.
Strain the hot broth over and finish with the egg and spring onion.
notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the whites are set and cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.
Use sliced chicken or tofu in place of ham.

recipes.title: Yemeni Shafut Yoghurt and Bread Salad
recipes.summary: A cool Yemeni dish of flatbread soaked in herby yoghurt with tomato, cucumber and chilli.
steps: Whisk the yoghurt with the garlic, chilli, half the herbs and the salt until smooth.
Lay half the torn bread in a large dish.
Spoon over half the yoghurt, then repeat with the remaining bread and yoghurt, and rest for 10 minutes, until the bread softens.
Scatter over the cucumber, tomato, onion and remaining herbs and finish with the oil.
notes: Serve straight away or the bread will turn mushy.

recipes.title: Saudi Jareesh Style Cracked Wheat Porridge
recipes.summary: A creamy Gulf cracked wheat and yoghurt porridge finished with sizzling cumin and onion butter.
steps: Simmer the cracked wheat in the water for 30 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and thick.
Add the milk and yoghurt and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Beat the porridge with a wooden spoon for 2 minutes, until smooth.
Fry the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, until deeply golden, then add the cumin.
Season the porridge with the salt and pepper and spoon into bowls with the cumin butter on top.
notes: Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon for a creamier texture.

recipes.title: Lebanese Fattet Hummus Chickpea and Bread Bowl
recipes.summary: Crisp pita pieces layered with warm chickpeas, garlicky yoghurt and sizzling pine nut butter.
steps: Bake the pita with the oil at 200°C for 8 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Warm the chickpeas in a small pan with a splash of water and the cumin for 5 minutes, until hot.
Whisk the yoghurt, tahini, garlic, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Melt the butter and toast the pine nuts for 3 minutes, until golden.
Layer the pita, chickpeas and yoghurt in bowls, then pour over the pine nut butter and scatter with the parsley.
notes: Serve straight away so the pita stays a little crisp.

recipes.title: Fijian Rourou Spinach in Coconut Cream
recipes.summary: Wilted greens simmered gently in coconut cream with onion, ginger and chilli, a classic Fijian side.
steps: Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the chilli and coconut cream and simmer for 4 minutes, until slightly reduced.
Add the spinach in handfuls and cook for 4 minutes, until wilted and tender.
Season with the lime juice and salt and serve with rice or root vegetables.
notes: Use frozen spinach, well squeezed, if fresh is unavailable.

recipes.title: Tahitian Cucumber and Tomato Coconut Salad
recipes.summary: A cooling salad of cucumber, tomato and red onion dressed in lime-spiked coconut cream.
steps: Salt the cucumber and onion for 5 minutes and drain off the liquid.
Whisk the coconut cream, lime juice, chilli and salt.
Toss the cucumber, tomato and onion with the dressing until well coated.
Scatter with coriander and serve chilled.
notes: Best eaten within an hour while crisp.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Sup Bap Sweetcorn and Egg Soup
recipes.summary: A silky chicken and sweetcorn soup with egg ribbons, popular as a Vietnamese street-side snack.
steps: Simmer the stock and half the sweetcorn for 8 minutes, until sweet and tender.
Blend the remaining sweetcorn with a little stock until smooth and stir into the pot.
Add the chicken and fish sauce and simmer for 3 minutes.
Mix the cornflour and water, stir in, and cook for 1 minute, until slightly thickened.
Pour in the egg in a thin stream while stirring, so it forms ribbons, then add the pepper.
Serve with spring onion and coriander.
notes: Food safety: make sure the chicken is piping hot at 75°C and the egg fully set before serving.
Skip the chicken for a vegetarian soup.

recipes.title: Korean Sujebi Hand-Torn Dough Soup
recipes.summary: Chewy hand-torn wheat dough flakes in an anchovy and kelp broth with zucchini, potato and spring onion.
steps: Knead the flour, water and oil into a smooth dough for 5 minutes, then rest for 30 minutes under a damp cloth.
Simmer the dashi, potato, onion and garlic for 10 minutes, until the potato is almost tender.
Stretch pieces of dough thin between your fingers and drop into the pot until all used.
Simmer for 8 minutes, until the dough floats and is chewy.
Add the zucchini, soy sauce and salt and cook for 3 minutes, then add the spring onion.
notes: Dough should be stretched very thin so it cooks quickly.
Check the dashi for fish if you need a vegetarian soup.
